benchmark.category: a restaurant point-of-sale back-office with insights and cancellation reporting
benchmark.users: restaurant owners and managers of the 'macha' outlet reviewing cancellations, staff notes and audit reports

requirements.source_phrase: Deploy the existing React frontend repo directly into `/app` and run it as-is, with no code edits.
requirements.statement: Opening the preview URL serves the MyGenie Core POS React app (its login screen) from the repo cloned into /app on port 3000, with no local source edits.
requirements.notes: Deployment is the first thing the user meets; the served preview must be the repo's own build, not a stub or a placeholder page.

requirements.source_phrase: Confirm the dev server compiles without fatal errors
requirements.statement: The dev server started from the repo's own script (craco start bound to 0.0.0.0:3000) compiles with no fatal error, answers 200 for / and for the main JS bundle, and serves the app again after a process restart or hot reload.
requirements.notes: The user's Phase 5 asks for the port check and for restart/hot-reload to work; a process that dies on reload fails the deployment.

requirements.source_phrase: Destination: `/app` (repo contents pulled directly into `/app`, not a subfolder)
requirements.statement: /app is a clone of https://github.com/Abhi-mygenie/core-pos-front-end-.git at branch main, with the repo contents at the top level of /app (no nested subfolder) and src/, public/ and package.json present.
requirements.notes: Repo and branch are named in the same user instruction; a nested clone would break the dev server and the build.

requirements.source_phrase: Platform files and folders preserved during the clear-and-clone
requirements.statement: The platform files preserved before the clear-and-clone (backend/.env, the .emergent markers, memory/test_credentials.md) are present in /app after the clone.
requirements.notes: Deleting these would lose the credentials file the later phases sign in with.

requirements.statement: The app reads REACT_APP_API_BASE_URL=https://preprod.mygenie.online/ and REACT_APP_SOCKET_URL from frontend/.env at build time and sends every API call to that host, with no host name written into the source.
requirements.notes: Every signed-in screen is empty without this; a hardcoded host would point the preview at the wrong environment.

requirements.statement: frontend/.env holds non-empty values for REACT_APP_FIREBASE_API_KEY, REACT_APP_FIREBASE_VAPID_KEY, REACT_APP_CRM_API_KEYS and REACT_APP_GOOGLE_MAPS_KEY, so Firebase, CRM and Maps initialise without a missing-key error on load.
requirements.notes: The four keys were the ones missing from the user's env block; the check is that they are present and used, and no key value is echoed into the UI, a log line or the repo.

requirements.statement: The login screen signs in with pms@macha.com / Qplazm@10 and lands the user in restaurant 69 'macha' with the Owner role.
requirements.notes: Seed credentials come from required_credentials (preview URL, preprod backend); no [USER] line names them, so the requirement is derived and every later phase signs in with exactly these values.

requirements.statement: The auth call to the configured preprod base URL returns a session for pms@macha.com / Qplazm@10 carrying restaurant 69 and role Owner, and a wrong password is refused with an error on the login screen and no session stored.
requirements.notes: External preprod backend; the app must surface a refusal rather than enter a half-signed-in state.

requirements.statement: On /reports-module/cancellations with the date range set to 2026-11-01 .. 2026-11-21, the existing REASON / NOTES cell of each row shows that row's staff cancellation note where the record has one.
requirements.notes: BUG-743: the row transform read only notes and never cancel_item_note, so a real staff note never reached the cell.

requirements.source_phrase: what about the cancellation report fix isnt that mentioned in handover by otheer investigation agent ?
requirements.statement: The cancellations endpoint for the requested range returns cancel_item_note on each row for both item-level and order-level rows, and a failed request surfaces as an error rather than a table of blank notes.
requirements.notes: The data contract: cancel_item_note is present per row (verified on preprod); the fallback field is notes.

requirements.source_phrase: this report page also have same issue right ?
requirements.statement: On /reports-module/cancel-detail the table has a Note column placed after Reason and before By, and each row shows that row's cancel_item_note in it.
requirements.notes: The user asked to confirm this page carries the same missing-data issue, then to do the intake. The '—' placeholder for an empty note is fixed by the build plan, not by a [USER] line.

requirements.source_phrase: this report page also have same issue right ?
requirements.statement: The cancel-detail data request for the range returns cancel_item_note on every row for both scope=item and scope=order, and a row with no note returns an empty value the page renders as '—'.
requirements.notes: Row objects already carry cancel_item_note via the spread; the check is that the field survives to the client for both scopes.

requirements.source_phrase: this two pages missing the data i think
requirements.statement: Both cancellation pages show the note for the same cancellation: a row whose note appears on /reports-module/cancellations also shows that note on /reports-module/cancel-detail, and neither page is left showing the reason only.
requirements.notes: The user's correction names exactly two pages; Order Note Audit is explicitly ruled out of scope in the same line.

requirements.source_phrase: this two pages missing the data i think
requirements.statement: For the same order and item, the cancellations report and the cancel-detail report return the same cancel_item_note value.
requirements.notes: Guards against one endpoint returning the note and the other dropping it.

requirements.statement: Downloading the Cancellations report for the current filter produces an Excel file and a PDF whose rows carry a Note column holding the same note the screen shows for that row.
requirements.notes: From features_or_bugs_to_test item 2 and the BUG-743 plan (export column at CancellationsMockup L420); the user's line only says the pages are missing the data.

requirements.statement: The export payload for the Cancellations report includes, for every row in the filtered range, a 'Note' column value taken from cancel_item_note (falling back to notes), and the downloaded file is generated from that payload.
requirements.notes: An export built from the DOM or from a different request than the table would silently drop the new column.

requirements.statement: Downloading the Item Cancellation Detail report produces an Excel file and a PDF whose header row includes a Note column after Reason and whose rows hold each row's note.
requirements.notes: From features_or_bugs_to_test item 4 and the BUG-743 plan (export column at CancelDetailMockup L106).

requirements.statement: The cancel-detail export payload includes key cancel_item_note labelled 'Note' after Reason for every exported row, and an empty note is written as the same placeholder the table shows.
requirements.notes: Column order in the export must match the table order the user specified (Reason then Note).

requirements.statement: With item-level cancellations (scope=item) and with full-order cancellations (scope=order), both report pages show the note on every row that has one.
requirements.notes: features_or_bugs_to_test item 5; a fix that only maps the item-level field would leave the order-level rows blank.

requirements.statement: The reports endpoints return cancel_item_note for scope=item and scope=order rows alike, so neither scope arrives with the note stripped.

With FROM=2026-11-01 and TO=2026-11-21 the Cancellations report lists a row for order #000021 carrying the item-level note 'item level notes', a row for order #000022, and rows whose note reads 'waiter got slapped'.
requirements.notes: Seed values come from features_or_bugs_to_test, the build's own QA notes, not from a [USER] line. If the preprod range holds no note rows, create a cancellation with a note first and re-check both pages.

requirements.statement: A cancellations row with neither cancel_item_note nor notes shows only its reason in the REASON / NOTES cell - no 'undefined', 'null', 'NaN' or dangling separator.
requirements.notes: Paranoid half of the note requirement: most rows have no note, so a broken fallback is the common case.

requirements.statement: The cancellations endpoint returns an empty string or null (never the literal string 'undefined') for cancel_item_note and notes on a row that has no note.
When cancel_item_note is empty but the record carries a value in notes, the REASON / NOTES cell on /reports-module/cancellations shows the notes value.
requirements.notes: The planned render is cancelItemNote || notes; without the fallback a legacy note vanishes.

requirements.statement: The cancellations response for a row whose cancel_item_note is empty and whose notes is set returns both fields with those values, so the page can resolve the fallback.
A cancel-detail row with an empty cancel_item_note renders '—' in the Note cell and the cell still sits between Reason and By.
requirements.notes: Placeholder fixed in the BUG-743 plan; a blank cell must not shift the By column.

requirements.statement: The cancel-detail payload keeps an explicit empty value for cancel_item_note rather than dropping the key, so the page can render its '—' placeholder per row.

Reloading either cancellation page, and opening it again in a new tab after signing in again, shows the same notes for the same range, so the note is read from the response and not held only in screen state.
requirements.notes: Paranoid form of 'the value is displayed': it must equal the stored value after a reload, not a value patched into local state.

requirements.statement: Repeating the cancellations and cancel-detail requests from a new session for the same range returns the same cancel_item_note values as the first session.

With a filter that matches no cancellations, /reports-module/cancel-detail shows a single empty-state row whose cell spans all 8 columns, the Note header still visible, and the TOTAL footer's filler spans so the layout does not shift.
requirements.notes: The plan bumps the empty-row colSpan 7 to 8 and the tfoot filler 3 to 4; a stale colSpan misaligns the new 8-column table - the exact regression the user asked to keep correct.

requirements.statement: The cancel-detail request for a range with no cancellations returns an empty list with a success status, not an error, so the page can render its empty state.
With a date range containing no cancellations, /reports-module/cancellations shows an explicit 'no data' state in place of the table, not a blank area or a spinner that never ends.
requirements.notes: Paranoid form of 'a list is shown': what it shows at zero rows.

requirements.statement: The cancellations request for a range with no rows returns an empty list and zeroed totals rather than an error.
Opening either cancellation report and downloading it writes nothing: after the export, every cancellation record's note and reason are unchanged when the page is reloaded.
requirements.notes: Reports are read-only; a display fix must not mutate a cancellation record.

requirements.statement: Opening /reports-module/cancellations or /reports-module/cancel-detail while signed out redirects to the login screen and renders no cancellation row, total or export control.
requirements.notes: A protected page renders blank or crashes if this is missing; the report routes are deep-linkable.

requirements.statement: A cancellations or cancel-detail request without a valid session is refused by the API and returns no row data.

The TOTAL footer on /reports-module/cancel-detail equals the sum of the amount column over the rows currently listed, in the same currency and precision, and the number of listed rows matches the rows shown.
requirements.notes: Class 1 business logic: adding a column must not disturb the footer, and the footer must stay true for the filtered row set.

requirements.statement: The cancel-detail response's totals equal the arithmetic sum of its rows' amounts to the cent and its row count equals the rows it returns.
The Cancellations report's totals and row count equal the rows listed for the chosen date range and change when the range changes.
requirements.notes: Class 1: a revenue figure that disagrees with its rows misleads the owner, who uses this report to chase lost sales.

requirements.statement: The cancellations response computes its totals and counts from the same filtered row set it returns, so no row is counted twice and none is omitted.

On /reports-module/cancel-detail the 8 columns including Note line up under their headers with no overlap or clipping at 1280px and at 375px width, and the Cancellations REASON / NOTES cell wraps a long note without pushing the row's other cells out of alignment.
requirements.notes: The user asked explicitly that table layout/alignment stay correct with the new column; a wrapped note is the realistic stress case.

requirements.statement: The report responses return the full note string untruncated, so the table and the export can show it whole.

Pressing the download control on either report shows that the export is running and then confirms the file was produced, the control returns to its idle state so it can be used again, and a failed export shows an error in the user's terms with no empty file offered.
requirements.notes: Class 2: nothing succeeds silently and nothing fails silently; the data-testid hooks are s28-download-trigger on cancel-detail and the download trigger on Cancellations.

requirements.statement: The export request returns a non-empty file of the requested type or a failure the client can report; it never returns an empty body with a success status.
Opening /reports-module/cancel-detail directly in a fresh tab loads the report with its filter and table, and the back arrow on that page returns to /cancellations.
requirements.notes: other_misc_info says the page is reached by the back-arrow drill or by direct URL; both must work.

requirements.statement: The cancel-detail route fires its data request with the default date range on a direct deep link and returns rows, so a cold load renders content rather than a blank page.

The chosen date range survives a reload and a back-navigation on both report pages and is applied to the table, the totals and the export, and a FROM later than TO is rejected with a message rather than silently showing an empty report.
requirements.notes: Class 3 state plus the paranoid date rule: an inverted range that silently reads as 'no cancellations' would hide real ones.

requirements.statement: Both report requests carry the FROM and TO the user selected, and the response for that range contains only rows whose cancellation date falls inside it.
Both report pages list only rows belonging to restaurant 69 'macha'; no cancellation, total or export row from another outlet appears while signed in as pms@macha.com.
requirements.notes: Class 4: the session is an outlet-scoped Owner account, so every listing, total and export must be scoped to that tenant.

requirements.statement: A cancellations or cancel-detail request from the restaurant-69 session returns no row belonging to another restaurant, including when another restaurant's order identifier is requested directly.
requirements.notes: Something private: a guessed identifier from outside the tenant must return nothing of the record.

requirements.statement: After signing out, the report screens make no further authenticated requests, and opening a report URL redirects to login.
requirements.notes: Class 4 session rule: the screen must not keep polling the reports with a dead session.

requirements.statement: A report request replaying the token from before sign-out is refused by the API and returns no row data.
For the same filter, the exported rows and Note values equal the rows and Note values the screen displays, once each and in the same order.
requirements.notes: Class 5/6: the export must be built from the same filtered result the table renders, not from a second, differently-parameterised request.

requirements.statement: The Excel download opens as a real .xlsx and the PDF as a valid .pdf, each with a header row that includes the Note column, under a file name that names the report and the date range.
requirements.notes: Class 6, worded by the file's content rather than by the response status.

requirements.statement: A row with no note is written to the export with the same placeholder the screen shows (empty cell or '—'), never the literal 'undefined' or 'null'.
requirements.notes: Most rows have no note, so a broken placeholder would fill the whole export.

requirements.statement: When the preprod API, the socket connection or a CRM call fails (bad key, timeout, non-2xx), the affected screen tells the user in their terms and does not render an empty report or zeroed totals as if the data were genuinely empty.
requirements.notes: Class 9: the app depends on external services whose keys the user supplied; a missing or rejected key must show, not fake an empty result.

requirements.statement: A failed or timed-out upstream call is surfaced to the client as an error the page can display, not swallowed into an empty successful payload.
The CRM API keys in frontend/.env are sent only to REACT_APP_CRM_BASE_URL; they are not logged to the console, embedded in a report export or sent to the reporting API.
requirements.notes: The user supplied CRM keys so CRM calls work; a key printed to the console or baked into a downloaded file is a leak.

requirements.statement: The cancellations and cancel-detail reports open, are left and reopened repeatedly without accumulating duplicate requests or subscriptions, and each reopen answers as fast as the first.
requirements.notes: Class 11: a report screen mounting sockets and pollers per visit leaks connections.

requirements.statement: The reports endpoints answer a full-year date range within a few seconds and page or cap their payload rather than streaming every cancellation row at once.
Every route the navigation reaches, including /reports-module/cancellations and /reports-module/cancel-detail, loads with no build error, missing module or undefined name in the browser console.
requirements.notes: Class 12: the deployment must compile cleanly; a console exception means the page is broken even if the shell renders.

requirements.statement: Both report pages offer a date range with presets and every table, total and export reflects the selected range, so a Nov 2026 range can be chosen in one step.
requirements.notes: benchmark: report screens in restaurant back-office tools ship a date range with presets that re-drive every widget on the page.

requirements.statement: The reports endpoints accept an explicit from/to range and return rows, totals and counts computed for exactly that window.
requirements.notes: benchmark: date-window reports compute their figures server-side for the chosen window.

requirements.statement: Each cancellation row names its order number, item, reason and the staff member and time of the cancellation, so a note can be traced back to the record that produced it.
requirements.notes: benchmark: cancellation reports identify the order and the staff member per row; a note with no order number is unusable for follow-up.

requirements.statement: Each cancellation row returned by the reports carries its order number, item name, reason, staff member and cancellation timestamp.
requirements.notes: benchmark: report rows carry the order and staff identity.

requirements.statement: Long reports page through their rows and every page keeps the same columns and the totals for the whole filtered range.
requirements.notes: benchmark: list reports page rather than render a thousand rows; the paranoid half of 'a list is shown at a thousand rows'.

requirements.statement: The reports endpoints page their results so each page holds a disjoint set of rows and every row of the range appears exactly once across the pages.
requirements.notes: benchmark: a paged report returns every matching row once.

requirements.statement: An order's diner name and mobile are captured and displayed separately from the order holder: editing the holder's name does not change the diner's, and both appear on the order view.
requirements.notes: From the CR-527 backend handover artifact the user uploaded and asked to read, probe and test; field names diner_name / diner_mobile are locked and the diner is plain text with no CRM link.

requirements.statement: The order payload stores and returns diner_name and diner_mobile as plain text independent of the order holder's name and mobile, and an order saved with them reads them back on reload.
requirements.notes: Pending FE work named in app_summary; identity rule: the diner and the holder are different entities even when their names match.

requirements.statement: OrderCard and the dashboard show the post-discount amount, which equals the pre-discount amount minus the applied discount, and the same value appears everywhere that order's total is shown.
requirements.notes: Pending FE work named in app_summary; Class 1 money rule - a discount shown in one place must move the total in every place it appears.

requirements.statement: The stored order carries the discounted total the app displays, computed from the pre-discount amount and the applied discount to the cent, and it is returned unchanged on reload.
requirements.notes: Pending FE work named in app_summary; a second discount application would double-count.
